definition: An alternative form of erne, an eagle or sea eagle.
example: In Scott’s verse, the earn near a tarn is an eagle; the spelling is an alternative form of erne.
usage: Bird noun. Erne can mean a sea eagle or, chiefly in poetic, regional or scientific use, an eagle more generally. The quotation does not identify a species.
distinctions: This valid alternative form names a bird. It is neither a spelling error to practise correcting nor a verb about receiving wages.

originalSense.definition: Alternative form of erne
originalSense.example:
They gleamed on many a dusky tarn ,
Haunted by the lonely earn

definition: EARN: the European Academic and Research Network, a former European academic computer network.
example: Capitalised EARN abbreviates European Academic and Research Network in this record.
usage: Historical network name used by universities and research institutions across Europe. The capitals identify an initialism.
distinctions: The initialism names the network, not a command to earn money or a certificate. It is not a generic label for every academic network.

originalSense.definition: Initialism of European Academic and Research Network: a former computer network connecting universities and research institutions across Europe.

definition: Earn: a river in Perth and Kinross, Scotland, flowing into the tidal River Tay.
example: The capitalised name Earn identifies the Scottish river that flows into the tidal River Tay.
usage: Geographical proper name. Use River Earn when a river name needs to be explicit.
distinctions: The river name is a separate proper-name record. It is unrelated to a person earning income and does not imply that the river is itself the Tay.

originalSense.definition: A river in Perth and Kinross council area, Scotland, which flows into the tidal River Tay.

definition: The latest time or date by which something must be completed.
example: The deadline for the essay is Friday at noon.
usage: Use by to say that work must arrive no later than the deadline: submit it by Friday at noon.
distinctions: A deadline is the final permitted time, not necessarily the day work begins or results are announced.

originalSense.definition: A time limit in the form of a date on or before which something must be completed.
originalSense.example: I must make this deadline or my boss will kill me!

distinctionTask.prompt: The essay must arrive by Friday at noon. This deadline is _____.
options: the date results will be announced
distinctionTask.explanation: The deadline tells you when submission must be completed, not when marking will finish.

definition: Necessary for something to happen, work or exist.
example: Clean water is essential for good health.
usage: Use essential for something or essential to something. Both can express necessity.
distinctions: In this meaning, essential means needed; useful describes a benefit without necessarily making something indispensable.

originalSense.definition: Necessary.
originalSense.example:
There’s canker at the root, your seed
Denies the blessing of the sun,
The light essential to your need.
Your hopes are murdered and undone.

distinctionTask.prompt: Clean water is essential for health. Here essential means _____.
distinctionTask.explanation: This use states a need, rather than merely saying that clean water is convenient.

definition: Comments or information that assess work, an activity or its results.
example: The tutor gave me detailed feedback on my essay.
usage: For comments on work, feedback is normally uncountable: some feedback or a piece of feedback.
distinctions: Feedback can include praise and suggestions as well as criticism. This meaning is separate from the howling sound produced by an audio loop.

originalSense.definition: Critical assessment of a process or activity or of their results.
originalSense.example: After you hand in your essays, I will give both grades and feedback.

distinctionTask.prompt: In ordinary study English: The tutor gave me _____ on my essay.
distinctionTask.explanation: Feedback is normally uncountable when it means comments on work; use some feedback or a piece of feedback.

definition: The act of allocating work or tasks to someone.
example: The assignment of tasks took place before the meeting.
usage: Assignment of tasks describes allocating the work; an assignment can separately mean the task a person receives.
distinctions: This meaning concerns the allocation process, not a particular piece of coursework.

originalSense.definition: The act of assigning; the allocation of a job or a set of tasks.
originalSense.example: This flow chart represents the assignment of tasks in our committee.

distinctionTask.prompt: The assignment of duties was completed before work began. Here assignment means _____.
options: a student essay that was submitted
distinctionTask.explanation: Assignment of duties names the act of distributing work, rather than an individual student task.

definition: A task given to students as homework or coursework.
example: The history assignment is due on Friday.
usage: Assignment is countable in this use: an assignment or two assignments. Homework is normally uncountable.
distinctions: A student assignment is the work to complete; it is not the act of allocating that work.

originalSense.definition: A task given to students, such as homework or coursework.
originalSense.example: Mrs Smith gave out our assignments, and said we had to finish them by Monday.

distinctionTask.prompt: In ordinary study English: I have two _____ to submit.
distinctionTask.explanation: Count individual pieces of student work as assignments. Homework is normally uncountable.

definition: A general overview of a subject or area.
example: The book gives a survey of recent research on sleep.
usage: A survey of a subject can summarise the field without asking people questions.
distinctions: An overview of earlier research differs from a survey that collects answers from respondents.

originalSense.definition: The act of surveying; a general view.
originalSense.example: Under his proud survey the city lies.

distinctionTask.prompt: This chapter is a survey of earlier research. It is _____.
options: a questionnaire for respondents to complete
distinctionTask.explanation: Here survey means an overview of research, rather than a form used to gather new answers.

definition: A study that collects information or opinions from a group of people.
example: The survey found that most students cycle to campus.
usage: Use a survey of a group or a survey about a topic. Results describe the people or data studied; they do not automatically establish a cause.
distinctions: The study and the questionnaire used to carry it out are related meanings. Conducting a survey refers to the investigation as a whole.

originalSense.definition: An examination of the opinions and/or information of a group of people.
originalSense.example: The local council conducted a survey of its residents to help it decide whether to go ahead with the roadside waste collection service.

distinctionTask.prompt: A survey of 300 students examined their travel habits. Here survey means _____.
options: a study collecting information from respondents
distinctionTask.answer: a study collecting information from respondents
distinctionTask.explanation: The students provide information about their habits; no land boundaries are being measured.

definition: A questionnaire or similar tool used to collect information or opinions.
example: Please complete the survey before leaving the workshop.
usage: Complete or fill in a survey when you are answering its questions.
distinctions: This use names the questionnaire itself. Survey can also name the whole study or an overview of a subject.

originalSense.definition: A questionnaire or similar instrument used for examining the opinions and/or information of a group of people.
originalSense.example: I just filled out that survey on roadside waste pick-up.

distinctionTask.prompt: Please fill in this survey. Survey refers to _____.
options: a written overview of earlier research
distinctionTask.explanation: Fill in asks the reader to supply answers on the questionnaire.

definition: To collect information about people by asking them questions.
example: We will survey local residents about the new bus route.
usage: Survey takes the people asked as its object: survey residents about their travel habits.
distinctions: This verb concerns asking people questions, rather than measuring a piece of land.

originalSense.definition: To investigate the opinions, experiences, etc., of people by asking them questions; to conduct a survey; to administer a questionnaire.

distinctionTask.prompt: The researchers will survey 200 residents about their travel habits. They will _____.
options: measure the boundaries of their land
distinctionTask.explanation: The stated topic is travel habits, so survey means gather answers from the residents.

definition: A piece of nonfiction writing in a newspaper, magazine, journal or similar publication.
example: The article explains how the new recycling system works.
usage: Use an article about or on a topic, or an article in a newspaper or journal.
distinctions: This is a piece of writing. It is separate from the grammar meaning of a, an or the.

originalSense.definition: A piece of nonfiction writing such as a story, report, opinion piece, or entry in a newspaper, magazine, journal, encyclopedia, etc.
originalSense.example: Although there are dozens of different types of gems, among the best known and most important are […]. (Common gem materials not addressed in this article include amber, amethyst, chalcedony, garnet, lazurite, malachite, opals, peridot, rhodonite, spinel, tourmaline, turquoise and zircon.)

distinctionTask.prompt: This magazine article discusses public transport. It is _____.
options: a grammatical word such as a or the
distinctionTask.explanation: A magazine article is a piece of writing; article has a different meaning in grammar.

definition: A grammatical word such as a, an or the that accompanies a noun.
example: In the phrase an old bridge, an is an indefinite article.
usage: A and an are indefinite articles; the is the definite article in English.
distinctions: The grammar meaning names a kind of word, not a newspaper or journal text.

originalSense.definition: A part of speech that indicates, specifies and limits a noun (a, an, or the in English). In some languages the article may appear as an ending (e.g. definite article in Swedish) or there may be none (e.g. Russian, Pashto).
originalSense.example:
‘A song called “Freak Like Me” by the Sugababes,’ said Jesse.
‘Just Sugababes, no article,’ the man said, enjoying the stunned reaction on Jesse’s face.

distinctionTask.prompt: In English grammar, an is an _____.
distinctionTask.explanation: An is an indefinite article; it is not an adverb.

definition: A group of people that leads, represents or governs an organisation or community.
example: The student council meets once a month.
usage: Council names a group or body. Do not confuse its spelling with counsel.
distinctions: Counsel can mean advice or a legal adviser; council is the governing or representative group in this example.

originalSense.definition: A committee that leads or governs (e.g. city council, student council).
originalSense.example: He turned back to the scene before him and the enormous new block of council dwellings. The design was some way after Corbusier but the block was built up on plinths and resembled an Atlantic liner swimming diagonally across the site.

distinctionTask.prompt: An elected body representing students is the student _____.
distinctionTask.explanation: The representative body is a student council. Counsel has separate advice and legal-adviser meanings.

definition: The surroundings and conditions that affect a person or thing.
example: The library provides a quiet environment for study.
usage: Use an environment for an activity, such as an environment for study.
distinctions: This broad meaning concerns surrounding conditions. The environment can separately mean the natural world.

originalSense.definition: The surroundings of, and influences on, a particular item of interest.
originalSense.example: What was seen from the top down, as a large environment with many difficult trade-offs, is instead seen from the bottom up--as 10 million microenvironments, each to be regulated in its own right. It is this inversion of perspective that distinguishes microgovernment from other kinds of regulation, and that accounts for its often-bizarre behavior.

distinctionTask.prompt: A quiet study environment refers to _____.
options: the surroundings and conditions for studying
distinctionTask.answer: the surroundings and conditions for studying
distinctionTask.explanation: This sentence concerns the conditions for study, which can include an indoor library.

definition: The natural world, including living things and their surroundings.
example: The policy aims to protect the environment from pollution.
usage: The environment commonly names the natural world as a whole.
distinctions: The natural-world meaning differs from a particular working, social or computing environment.

originalSense.definition: The natural world or ecosystem.
originalSense.example: It is tempting to speculate about the incentives or compulsions that might explain why anyone would take to the skies in [the] basket [of a balloon]: […]; […]; or perhaps to muse on the irrelevance of the borders that separate nation states and keep people from understanding their shared environment.

distinctionTask.prompt: This policy protects the environment by reducing river pollution. Here environment means _____.
options: the software installed on a laptop
distinctionTask.explanation: River pollution concerns the natural world, not a computer system.

definition: The money or other resources available for a particular purpose or period.
example: Our budget for the trip is £300.
usage: Use a budget of an amount and a budget for a purpose. Staying within budget means not spending more than allowed.
distinctions: This meaning names the available amount. A budget can separately mean the plan listing expected income and spending.

originalSense.definition: The amount of money or resources earmarked for a particular institution, activity or timeframe.
originalSense.example: limited budget
wordFamily: champagne taste on a beer budget

distinctionTask.prompt: The team has a budget of £300 for travel. Budget refers to _____.
options: the amount available for planned spending
distinctionTask.answer: the amount available for planned spending
distinctionTask.explanation: The budget is an available allowance; the sentence does not say that the money has already been spent.

definition: A plan listing expected income and intended spending.
example: The treasurer prepared a budget showing expected income and planned spending.
usage: A budget is a plan. Actual income and spending may differ from its estimates.
distinctions: This use names the financial plan, rather than just the amount of money available.

originalSense.definition: An itemized summary of intended expenditure; usually coupled with expected revenue.
wordFamily: champagne taste on a beer budget

distinctionTask.prompt: An annual budget lists expected income and planned expenses. Here budget is _____.
options: a pile of cash already received
distinctionTask.explanation: This meaning concerns planned income and expenditure, not money already received.

definition: The tools, machines or other items needed for a particular activity.
example: The laboratory needs new safety equipment.
usage: Equipment is normally uncountable in everyday study and work English: some equipment or a piece of equipment.
distinctions: Count individual items as pieces of equipment. Older or specialist countable uses do not make equipments the usual wording for ordinary tools.

originalSense.definition: Any items used in equipping something or someone, for example things needed for an expedition or voyage.
originalSense.example: We need more gardening equipment if we want to properly landscape our yard, not just a rake and some gloves.

distinctionTask.prompt: Choose the usual wording in a modern lab report: The lab bought _____.
distinctionTask.explanation: Equipment is normally uncountable in this use. Count individual items with pieces of equipment.

previousSenses.definition: The tools, machines or other items needed for a particular activity.
previousSenses.example: The laboratory needs new safety equipment.

definition: A duplicate of an original document, image or other object.
example: Please keep a copy of the completed form.
usage: Copy is countable in this meaning: one copy or two copies.
distinctions: A copy is the duplicate. The original is the document or object from which it was made.

originalSense.definition: The result of copying; an identical or nearly identical duplicate of an original.
originalSense.example: Please bring me at least 200 copies of this report. The photocopier is down the hall on the right.

distinctionTask.prompt: The original form stays in the office; I keep a copy. My copy is _____.
distinctionTask.explanation: A copy duplicates the original form; it is not that original.

definition: To sell something at a reduced price.
example: The shop will discount winter coats at the end of the season.
usage: This verb takes the item being sold as its object.
distinctions: Discounting a product concerns its price. Discounting a warning instead means treating it as unimportant.

originalSense.definition: To sell at a reduced price.
originalSense.example: Sales were slow even after the shop discounted the product.

distinctionTask.prompt: The shop will discount a £50 coat to £40. It will _____.
options: sell it at a lower price
distinctionTask.answer: sell it at a lower price
distinctionTask.explanation: The selling price falls from £50 to £40, so discount means sell at a reduced price.

definition: A reduction in the usual price.
example: Students get a discount on museum tickets.
usage: Use a discount on an item or service, or buy something at a discount.
distinctions: The noun names the price reduction; the verb discount can describe selling at that reduced price.

originalSense.definition: A reduction in price.
originalSense.example: For the summer sale, there was 40% discount in all the stores at the mall.

distinctionTask.prompt: A ticket costs £8 instead of £10 because of a student discount. The discount is _____.
distinctionTask.explanation: The discount lowers the price; it does not add a charge.

definition: To disregard something or treat it as unimportant.
example: We should not discount the possibility of further delays.
usage: Not discount a possibility means keep it under consideration; it does not say that it is certain.
distinctions: This meaning concerns how seriously information is treated, rather than a reduction in a selling price.

originalSense.definition: To disregard or regard as unimportant.
originalSense.example: Owing to his reputation, they discounted his comments.

distinctionTask.prompt: We should not discount her warning. We should not _____.
options: buy it at a reduced price
distinctionTask.explanation: A warning is information to consider, so discount here means disregard or treat as unimportant.

definition: To deduct an amount from an account, debt or charge.
example: In the source's rare construction discount five per cent for prompt payment, discount means deduct that percentage from the amount due.
collocations: discount five per cent for prompt payment
usage: Rare in this deduct construction. Deduct an amount from a bill is clearer in ordinary present-day writing.
distinctions: Here the object is the amount deducted; in discount a product, the object is the item sold more cheaply.

originalSense.definition: To deduct from an account, debt, charge, etc.
originalSense.example: Merchants sometimes discount five or six per cent for prompt payment of bills.

definition: To advance money on a bill or note after deducting interest before it is due.
example: The bank agreed to discount a £1,000 bill, advancing £970 before it fell due.
usage: Finance. The holder receives money before maturity, with interest deducted in advance.
distinctions: The £30 difference in this example is a monetary deduction. It is not an annual interest rate.

distinctionTask.prompt: A bank will discount a £1,000 bill by advancing £970 before maturity. The £30 difference is _____.
options: an annual rate of 30 per cent
distinctionTask.explanation: The difference is £1,000 minus £970. No annual rate can be inferred without a time period and calculation convention.

originalSense.definition: To lend money upon, deducting the discount or allowance for interest.
originalSense.example: The banks discount notes and bills of exchange.

definition: To anticipate an event and take its expected effect into account in advance.
example: Investors already discount a fall in profits when valuing these shares.
usage: Often used of markets or expectations. An anticipated effect can be reflected in a price before the event occurs.
distinctions: Discount can mean take into account in advance here. In discount a warning, it instead means disregard. Context matters.

distinctionTask.prompt: Share prices already discount a fall in profits. Investors have _____.
options: taken the expected fall into account
treated the expected fall as irrelevant
distinctionTask.answer: taken the expected fall into account
distinctionTask.explanation: In this market use, the anticipated change is already reflected in valuation.

originalSense.definition: To take into consideration beforehand; to anticipate and form conclusions concerning (an event).
originalSense.example: The market has dropped, discounting changes in interest rates.

definition: In transactional analysis, to disregard the content of another person's communication in one's response.
example: In ITAA's account of a discount transaction, a response disregards the content of the communication it answers.
usage: Transactional-analysis terminology. ITAA describes this communication pattern; this reading note does not offer a diagnosis or a complete account of every use of discounting.
distinctions: The professional description concerns disregarded communication. It does not define the term simply as one person's feelings being more important than reality.

originalSense.definition: To believe, or act as though one believes, that one's own feelings are more important than the reality of a situation.

definition: Interest deducted in advance from the amount of a bill or note before it is due.
example: For a bill with a face amount of £1,000, the bank advances £970 and retains a discount of £30.
usage: Finance. This meaning names the amount deducted in advance.
distinctions: A discount amount is measured in money; a discount rate is a rate used to calculate a deduction.

distinctionTask.prompt: A £1,000 bill produces a £970 advance. The discount amount is _____.
distinctionTask.explanation: The amount is £1,000 minus £970 = £30. An annual rate requires the term and rate convention.

originalSense.definition: A deduction made for interest, in advancing money upon, or purchasing, a bill or note not due; payment in advance of interest upon money.

definition: The interest rate charged when a bill or note is discounted.
example: The bank quoted a discount rate of 6 per cent per year for the bill.
usage: Finance. State the rate and its time basis. Calculating a monetary deduction also requires the amount, term and convention.
distinctions: This meaning is a rate, not the sum of money deducted. A bare percentage does not supply a time period.

distinctionTask.prompt: In a quoted discount rate of 6 per cent per year, discount refers to _____.
distinctionTask.explanation: The quotation states a percentage with an annual time basis, not a monetary amount.

originalSense.definition: The rate of interest charged in discounting.

definition: A lack, disadvantage or shortcoming.
example: In the preserved Dickens passage, being at such a discount in looks and composure means being at a disadvantage in those respects.
collocations: at a discount in respect of something
usage: Figurative reading use in the cited literary passage. The retained quotation is about appearance and composure.
distinctions: This passage describes a disadvantage; it does not say that the speaker is being sold at a lower price.

originalSense.definition: A lack or shortcoming.
originalSense.example: On our approaching the house where the Misses Spenlow lived, I was at such a discount in respect of my personal looks and presence of mind, that Traddles proposed a gentle stimulant in the form of a glass of ale.

definition: In transactional analysis, a response that disregards the content of another person's communication.
example: ITAA uses discount transaction for a response that disregards the content of the communication it answers.
usage: Transactional-analysis terminology. This communication-specific description is supported by ITAA's core concepts; it is not a diagnosis.
distinctions: This specialist noun concerns a response in communication, not a retail saving or an interest deduction.

originalSense.definition: The act of one who believes, or act as though they believe, that their own feelings are more important than the reality of a situation.

definition: Specializing in selling goods at reduced prices.
example: We bought the stationery from a discount store.
usage: Used before a noun to describe a retailer or store selling goods at reduced prices.
distinctions: Discount describes the retailer here. It does not mean that every item is cheaper than every competitor's item.

distinctionTask.prompt: A discount store is a store that specializes in _____.
distinctionTask.explanation: The adjective describes the store's retail business, not bill discounting.

originalSense.definition: Specializing in selling goods at reduced prices.
originalSense.example: If you're looking for cheap clothes, there's a discount clothier around the corner.

definition: An examination to establish the condition, quantity or quality of something.
example: The building survey identified cracks in the roof supports.
usage: This examination can concern buildings, roads, supplies or other physical items.
distinctions: A building survey examines the property; it need not ask a group of people for opinions.

distinctionTask.prompt: A building survey finds cracks in the roof. Here survey means _____.
options: an examination of the building's condition
distinctionTask.answer: an examination of the building's condition
distinctionTask.explanation: The survey examines the property's physical condition.

originalSense.definition: A particular view; an examination, especially an official examination, of a particular group of items, in order to ascertain the condition, quantity, or quality.
originalSense.example: A survey of the stores of a ship; a survey of roads and bridges; a survey of buildings.

definition: The operation of measuring the contours, dimensions or position of an area of land.
example: The survey took two days of measurements before the team drew the boundary plan.
usage: Land measurement. This meaning names the work of measuring the area.
distinctions: The measuring operation differs from the measured plan produced from it. Both can be called a survey.

distinctionTask.prompt: The survey took two days of measurements before the plan was drawn. Survey names _____.
distinctionTask.explanation: The sentence describes measurement work that precedes drawing the plan.

originalSense.definition: The operation of finding the contour, dimensions, position, or other particulars of any part of the Earth's surface.

definition: A measured plan and description of an area of land.
example: The survey attached to the deed shows the plot's measured boundaries.
collocations: a survey attached to a deed
usage: Land measurement. This use names the resulting plan or document.
distinctions: A survey can be the measuring work or its resulting plan. Attached to the deed identifies the document here.

distinctionTask.prompt: The survey attached to the deed shows measured boundaries. Here survey is _____.
distinctionTask.explanation: A document attached to a deed is the resulting plan, not the measuring operation.

originalSense.definition: A measured plan and description of any portion of country.
originalSense.example: The owners of the adjoining plots had conflicting surveys.

definition: An auction at which a farm is let on a lease lasting for specified lives.
example: In this historical farm-letting use, a survey is an auction for a lease for lives, not a sale of the farm outright.
collocations: a survey for a farm lease
usage: Historical. A lease for lives is tied to specified people's lifetimes; the term is not a modern questionnaire.
distinctions: The auction grants a lease of the farm. It does not necessarily transfer ownership of the farm.

originalSense.definition: An auction at which a farm is let for a lease for lives.

definition: In US customs terminology, a district for collecting customs under a particular officer.
example: In the source's US customs use, survey names the collection district under an officer, not a set of questionnaire responses.
usage: US customs terminology. This source meaning identifies a district; it does not establish the name or status of any current agency unit.
distinctions: Customs here concerns duties on imported or exported goods. The meaning is geographic or administrative, not public-opinion research.

originalSense.definition: A district for the collection of customs under a particular officer.

definition: To look carefully over an area, especially from a high place.
example: From the ridge, we paused to survey the valley below.
usage: The object is the area or scene being viewed.
distinctions: Looking over a valley does not by itself mean measuring its boundaries or asking its residents questions.

distinctionTask.prompt: From the ridge, we survey the valley below. Here survey means _____.
distinctionTask.explanation: The viewpoint describes attentive looking, without claiming a measurement operation.

originalSense.definition: To inspect, or take a view of; to view with attention, as from a high place; to overlook
originalSense.example: He stood on a hill, and surveyed the surrounding country.

definition: To examine something closely or critically.
example: Before choosing a method, the team will survey the available evidence.
usage: Use a direct object for the material examined: survey the evidence.
distinctions: Examining evidence can include reviewing documents; it does not necessarily involve a questionnaire.

distinctionTask.prompt: The team will survey the available evidence before choosing a method. It will _____.
options: ask the evidence to complete a questionnaire
distinctionTask.explanation: The object is material to examine, not people to question.

originalSense.definition: To view with a scrutinizing eye; to examine.
originalSense.example: […]with ſuch alter'd Looks,[…] / All pale, and ſpeechleſs, he ſurvey'd me round;

definition: To inspect something in order to establish its condition, situation or value.
example: A qualified surveyor will survey the house for structural defects.
usage: Property inspection. The object is the property; for can introduce the defects being sought.
distinctions: Inspecting a house for defects differs from surveying the owners about their opinions.

distinctionTask.prompt: A surveyor will survey the house for structural defects, examining _____.
distinctionTask.explanation: The stated purpose is to inspect the building for defects.

originalSense.definition: To examine with reference to condition, situation, value, etc.; to examine and ascertain the state of
originalSense.example: It was his job to survey buildings in order to determine their value and risks.

definition: To measure and map the form, extent or position of land using linear and angular measurements.
example: Engineers will survey the site with measuring instruments before drawing the plan.
usage: Surveying. The work uses measurements to establish the shape, extent or position of the area.
distinctions: This is measurement work. Merely looking over the site from a hill does not establish those measured dimensions.

distinctionTask.prompt: Engineers survey a site using linear and angular measurements. They _____.
distinctionTask.explanation: The instruments and measurements identify the land-surveying use.

originalSense.definition: To determine the form, extent, position, etc., of, as a tract of land, a coast, harbor, or the like, by means of linear and angular measurements, and the application of the principles of geometry and trigonometry
originalSense.example: to survey land or a coast

definition: To examine a manor's boundaries and rights, its tenants' tenure, and its rents and value.
example: In the manorial use, to survey an estate includes examining its boundaries, estate rights, tenancies, rents and value.
usage: Manorial administration and source reading. Royalties in the imported gloss refers to estate rights, not authors' publishing payments.
distinctions: This is a detailed examination of an estate and its tenures. The cited old passage does not by itself establish that every use of the verb is obsolete.

originalSense.definition: To examine and ascertain, as the boundaries and royalties of a manor, the tenure of the tenants, and the rent and value of the same.
originalSense.example: all the Tenants Leases and Copies are surveyed

definition: An informal word for a photocopy.
example: Please make a Xerox of the signed page.
usage: Informal copy noun. Photocopy is a more neutral choice in formal writing.
distinctions: This noun names a copy of a document; the same spelling also has a separate copying-verb use.

distinctionTask.prompt: Please make a Xerox of the signed page. Here Xerox names _____.
distinctionTask.explanation: The object made is a copy, rather than a signature.

originalSense.definition: A xerograph (copy).
originalSense.example: Near-synonyms: photocopy (broadly synonymous), photostat (broadly synonymous)

definition: Plural of accountant: people who maintain or examine accounts and records.
example: The accountants checked the company's financial records.
usage: Plural noun: the accountants are; one accountant is. The financial-record context identifies the profession here.
distinctions: Accountants names people. Accounts can name the records they keep; the two words are not interchangeable.

distinctionTask.prompt: The accountants checked the records. Accountants refers to _____.
distinctionTask.explanation: The plural noun identifies the people performing the check.

originalSense.definition: plural of accountant
originalSense.example: For quotations using this term, see Citations:accountants.

definition: A cylindrical container, often made from wooden staves held together by hoops.
example: They stored rainwater in a wooden barrel.
usage: Countable container noun. A barrel can also name a quantity; the amount depends on the commodity and convention.
distinctions: The wooden barrel in this sentence is the physical container. The sentence does not define a standard unit of volume.

distinctionTask.prompt: They stored rainwater in a wooden barrel. Barrel names _____.
distinctionTask.explanation: A physical container is described; no volume convention or capacity is supplied.

originalSense.definition: A round (cylindrical) vessel, such as a cask, of greater length than breadth, and bulging in the middle, made of staves bound with hoops, and having flat ends (heads). The word is sometimes applied to a similar cylindrical container made of metal, usually called a drum.
originalSense.example: Near-synonym: cask

definition: One of the small balls threaded together on a rosary or similar string of prayer beads.
example: She moved one bead along the rosary as she prayed.
usage: Countable religious-use noun. One bead is a part of the string, rather than the entire rosary.
distinctions: This exact meaning is a prayer bead. A decorative bead on a necklace is a separate broader use.

distinctionTask.prompt: She moved one bead along the rosary. Here one bead is _____.
options: one small part of the string
distinctionTask.answer: one small part of the string
distinctionTask.explanation: The singular noun refers to one threaded ball.

originalSense.definition: Each in a string of small balls making up the rosary or paternoster.
originalSense.example: Holonym: prayer beads

definition: A long-handled brush used for sweeping floors and other surfaces.
example: Use a broom to sweep the kitchen floor.
usage: Countable noun for the cleaning tool. Broom also has separate plant-related meanings.
distinctions: A broom sweeps loose material; a mop is normally used for cleaning with liquid.

distinctionTask.prompt: To sweep loose dust from a dry floor, use a _____.
distinctionTask.explanation: A broom is the sweeping tool; a bucket alone does not sweep.

originalSense.definition: A domestic utensil with fibers bound together at the end of a long handle, used for sweeping.
originalSense.example: Meronyms: broomstick (handle), bavin (head)

definition: An artillery assembly including a tube and its breech or firing mechanism.
example: The museum displayed a cannon alongside other artillery equipment.
usage: Artillery terminology. This source meaning names an assembly used as a component of a gun, howitzer or mortar.
distinctions: Cannon with two n letters in the middle concerns artillery here. Canon has separate uses for rules, accepted works or musical composition.

distinctionTask.prompt: The museum displayed a cannon with other artillery equipment. Cannon refers to _____.
options: an accepted set of literary works
distinctionTask.explanation: Artillery identifies cannon; an accepted body of works can be called a canon.

originalSense.definition: A complete assembly, consisting of an artillery tube and a breech mechanism, firing mechanism or base cap, which is a component of a gun, howitzer or mortar, which may include muzzle appendages.
originalSense.example: Holonyms: gun, field gun; howitzer; mortar

definition: A grammatical unit containing a subject and a verb, which may be a whole sentence or part of one.
example: The clause "the train arrived" contains a subject and a verb.
usage: This is the grammatical meaning. In the example, the train is the subject and arrived is the verb.
distinctions: A clause may form an entire sentence or be part of a longer sentence; clause and sentence are not always interchangeable.

distinctionTask.prompt: In "We waited because the train was late", "because the train was late" is _____.
options: a clause within a longer sentence
distinctionTask.answer: a clause within a longer sentence
distinctionTask.explanation: The because-clause is one part of the complete sentence.

originalSense.definition: A group of words that contains a subject and a verb; it may be part of a sentence or may constitute the whole sentence, depending on the syntax in each instance.
originalSense.example: Near-synonyms: sentential, sentence

definition: Preparations applied to the body to change or enhance its appearance.
example: The shop sells cosmetics such as lipstick and mascara.
usage: Plural noun in this meaning: these cosmetics are. Cosmetic can also be an adjective, as in cosmetic products.
distinctions: Cosmetics names the products. Cosmetic as an adjective describes something and does not by itself name the plural products.

distinctionTask.prompt: The shop sells cosmetics such as lipstick. Cosmetics names _____.
options: all clothing sold in the shop
distinctionTask.explanation: The listed products identify the appearance-related preparations.

originalSense.definition: Preparations applied externally to change or enhance the beauty of skin, hair, nails, lips, and eyes.
originalSense.example: Near-synonyms: makeup, make-up; beauty products

definition: Plural of criterion: standards or requirements used to judge or compare things.
example: The selection criteria include relevant experience and clear communication.
usage: For the ordinary plural meaning, write the criteria are; use criterion for one standard. Other source usages remain separately available.
distinctions: The imported plural meaning concerns several standards. It is distinct from the separately recorded singular use of criteria.

distinctionTask.prompt: In ordinary edited English, several selection _____.
distinctionTask.explanation: Criteria is the ordinary plural; criterion is singular.

originalSense.definition: plural of criterion
originalSense.example: For quotations using this term, see Citations:criteria.

definition: A non-soap cleaning agent, especially one containing a synthetic surfactant.
example: Add detergent to the washing machine before starting the wash.
usage: The word can name the cleaning substance without an article, as in add detergent, or a type or product, as in a mild detergent.
distinctions: This source meaning excludes soap. Cleaner is broader and need not identify the substance as a detergent.

distinctionTask.prompt: A non-soap washing agent is called a _____.
distinctionTask.explanation: Detergent names the cleaning agent; the machine is the equipment.

originalSense.definition: Any non-soap cleaning agent, especially a synthetic surfactant.
originalSense.example: Near-synonym: cleaner (sometimes coordinate)

definition: A comfortable room in a home used for everyday relaxation and leisure.
example: The children watched a film in the family room.
usage: This exact meaning concerns a room in a dwelling, rather than a hotel room offered for a family.
distinctions: Family room and living room can overlap in ordinary home descriptions. Their names do not guarantee different layouts or functions.

distinctionTask.prompt: In a house, a family room is used for _____.
distinctionTask.explanation: The home context identifies a leisure room in a dwelling.

originalSense.definition: A comfortable room in a dwelling, for frequent leisure use.
originalSense.example: Near-synonyms: den, rec room, playroom, game room

definition: A sticky substance used to join materials together.
example: Apply glue to the cardboard and press the pieces together.
usage: Usually a substance noun here. A glue can identify a particular type of adhesive.
distinctions: Glue is the adhesive material; to glue is a separate verb meaning join with an adhesive.

distinctionTask.prompt: Apply glue to join the cardboard pieces. Glue names _____.
distinctionTask.explanation: The noun is the substance applied to the cardboard.

originalSense.definition: A hard gelatin made by boiling bones and hides, used in solution as an adhesive; or any sticky adhesive substance.
originalSense.example: Near-synonyms: adhesive, cement

definition: As a secondary or unintended result, rather than as the main purpose.
example: The survey incidentally revealed a drainage problem while measuring the site.
usage: Manner/result adverb in this meaning. The drainage finding is a side result of the survey, rather than its stated measuring purpose.
distinctions: Sentence-opening Incidentally can introduce an aside in conversation. That discourse use is separately recorded.

distinctionTask.prompt: The survey incidentally revealed a problem while measuring the site. The finding was _____.
distinctionTask.explanation: Incidentally marks the discovery as secondary to the measuring work.

originalSense.definition: In an incidental manner.
originalSense.example: Near-synonyms: coincidentally, happenstantially, circumstantially, by chance, accidentally, semirandomly, randomly

definition: Animals kept on a farm, such as cattle, sheep or pigs.
example: The farm keeps livestock including cattle and sheep.
usage: Collective farm-animal noun. Use an animal or a head of livestock when an individual count must be explicit.
distinctions: Livestock identifies farm animals here; crops are plants rather than livestock.

distinctionTask.prompt: The farm raises livestock such as _____.
distinctionTask.explanation: Cattle and sheep are farm animals; wheat and barley are crops.

originalSense.definition: Farm animals; animals domesticated for cultivation.
originalSense.example: Meronym: stock animal

definition: A room in a home used for socialising and leisure.
example: We sat in the living room and talked after dinner.
usage: Countable room noun. Living is part of the compound name here, rather than a claim that the room itself is alive.
distinctions: Living room and family room can overlap in home descriptions; a strict difference is not implied by either name.

distinctionTask.prompt: We sat and talked in the living room. Living room names _____.
options: a room for social and leisure activities
a room that is itself alive
distinctionTask.answer: a room for social and leisure activities
distinctionTask.explanation: The compound refers to a room used by people for everyday activities.

originalSense.definition: A room in a private house used for general social and leisure activities.
originalSense.example: Near-synonyms: lounge (esp. UK), loungeroom, lounge room (esp. Australia), sitting room, parlour, parlor, foreroom, front room, drawing room, zitkamer

definition: A written character or symbol that represents a word or phrase.
example: A logogram represents a word or phrase rather than a single speech sound.
usage: Writing-system terminology. The source includes characters as well as symbols; a logogram need not be a picture of its meaning.
distinctions: A logogram represents a word or phrase. An individual alphabetic letter commonly represents a sound or part of a sound pattern.

distinctionTask.prompt: A logogram represents _____.
options: only one speech sound by definition
distinctionTask.explanation: The lexical unit represented distinguishes the logogram in this definition.

originalSense.definition: A character or symbol (usually nonalphanumeric) that represents a word or phrase.
originalSense.example: Near-synonyms: (polysemic, sometimes synonymous) lexigram; lexigraph

definition: A party or gathering at which people wear masks and costumes.
example: Guests wore elaborate masks to the masquerade.
usage: Countable party noun in this meaning. The word also has a separate figurative use for a deceptive appearance.
distinctions: A masquerade party involves masks and costumes; the sentence does not accuse the guests of deception.

distinctionTask.prompt: Guests wore masks to the masquerade. Masquerade names _____.
distinctionTask.explanation: The party context identifies the literal gathering.

originalSense.definition: An assembly or party of people wearing (usually elaborate or fanciful) masks and costumes, and amusing themselves with dancing, conversation, or other diversions.
originalSense.example: Near-synonym: costume party

definition: A person sent to carry out a mission.
example: In this broad source meaning, a missionary is someone sent on a mission; the definition does not specify the mission's purpose.
collocations: a missionary sent on a mission
usage: Reading guidance for the broad source meaning. The dictionary separately records a person who spreads a religion.
distinctions: The broad mission sense and the religion-specific sense remain separate; a mission's purpose must come from context.

originalSense.definition: One who is sent on a mission.
originalSense.example: Near-synonym: emissary

definition: A machine or device that produces motion or converts another form of energy into mechanical energy.
example: An electric motor drives the pump.
usage: Countable device noun. Electric in this example identifies the kind of motor; it is not a requirement for every dictionary use.
distinctions: An electric motor converts electrical input into mechanical motion; a generator performs the reverse energy-conversion role.

distinctionTask.prompt: An electric motor driving a pump provides _____.
distinctionTask.explanation: The motor supplies motion to drive the pump.

originalSense.definition: A machine or device that converts other energy forms into mechanical energy, or imparts motion.
originalSense.example: Near-synonyms: drive, engine (sometimes synonymous)

definition: A document itemising the contents of each package in a shipment.
example: The packing list records the contents and weight of each carton.
usage: Logistics and transport. The International Trade Administration describes a package-by-package list including weights, measurements and goods.
distinctions: This is a shipment-contents document. It is distinct from a personal checklist of items to take on holiday.

distinctionTask.prompt: For an export shipment, the packing list itemises _____.
distinctionTask.explanation: The logistics document identifies what each package contains.

originalSense.definition: (logistics, transport)
originalSense.example: Near-synonym: shipping list

definition: Pan, the Greek god associated with nature, often depicted as part goat and part man playing pipes.
example: The capitalised name Pan refers here to the Greek god of nature, rather than a cooking utensil.
usage: Proper-name reading guidance. This source identity comes from the page Pan; the ordinary lowercase cooking noun is kept separately.
distinctions: Capitalised Pan in this meaning names a deity. Lowercase pan can name a cooking vessel.

originalSense.definition: Greek god of nature, often visualized as half goat and half man playing pipes.
originalSense.example: Near-synonyms: Faunus, Pales (Roman counterparts, not identical)

definition: A restatement of a text or idea in different words.
example: Her paraphrase kept the main idea but changed the wording.
usage: Countable restatement noun. The verb paraphrase is a separate use of the same spelling.
distinctions: A paraphrase changes the wording while aiming to retain the meaning; a direct quotation retains the quoted wording.

distinctionTask.prompt: A paraphrase of a sentence uses _____.
options: different wording to retain its meaning
the exact wording as a direct quotation
distinctionTask.answer: different wording to retain its meaning
distinctionTask.explanation: Changing wording while retaining meaning identifies a paraphrase.

originalSense.definition: A restatement of a text in different words, often to clarify meaning or from memory rather than verbatim.
originalSense.example: Near-synonym: paraphrasis

definition: To produce a paper copy of a computer document; print out.
example: Please print off two copies of the timetable.
usage: Separable phrasal verb: print off the document or print the document off. With a pronoun, use print it off.
distinctions: Print off concerns producing a paper copy here. It does not mean deleting the computer document.

distinctionTask.prompt: Please print off the timetable. You should _____.
distinctionTask.explanation: The phrasal verb concerns printing the document.

originalSense.definition: Synonym of print out.
originalSense.example: Near-synonym: run off

definition: Public communication intended to influence an audience and advance an agenda.
example: The campaign used propaganda to promote its political agenda.
usage: Usually a mass noun in this communication meaning. The source labels neutral usage dated; the word often carries a critical implication.
distinctions: Calling material propaganda describes its persuasive purpose or framing. It does not by itself establish that every statement in it is false.

distinctionTask.prompt: The campaign used propaganda to advance an agenda. Its stated purpose was to _____.
distinctionTask.explanation: The definition concerns communication serving an agenda.

originalSense.definition: Agitation, publicity, public communication aimed at influencing an audience and furthering an agenda.
originalSense.example: Near-synonym: public diplomacy (sometimes asserted to be synonymous)

definition: Based on quantities or numbers, especially in measurement or data.
example: The study uses quantitative data such as journey times and passenger counts.
usage: Adjective. The numeric examples show what is measured or counted; they do not establish the data's accuracy.
distinctions: Quantitative concerns quantities. Qualitative concerns qualities or characteristics; neither label alone guarantees better evidence.

distinctionTask.prompt: Journey times and passenger counts are examples of _____ data.
distinctionTask.explanation: The examples are numerical measurements and counts.

originalSense.definition: Of a measurements and data types: based on some quantity or number rather than on some quality.
originalSense.example: Near-synonyms: nonqualitative, unqualitative

definition: A cutting tool with two blades joined at a pivot, usually used as a plural noun.
example: These scissors are sharp enough to cut the fabric.
usage: For the usual tool meaning, write these scissors are, or this pair of scissors is.
distinctions: Scissors names the tool; a pair of scissors is one complete tool, rather than two separate tools.

distinctionTask.prompt: In ordinary edited English, this pair of scissors _____ sharp.
distinctionTask.explanation: Pair is the singular head of this noun phrase, so this pair is sharp.

originalSense.definition: A tool used for cutting thin material, consisting of two crossing blades attached at a pivot point in such a way that the blades slide across each other when the handles are closed.
originalSense.example: Near-synonym: shears

definition: A continuous range between possible extremes.
example: The survey captured a broad spectrum of opinions.
usage: Figurative range noun in this example. The source also contains separate technical meanings concerning light and other phenomena.
distinctions: A spectrum of opinions describes a range of views. It is not an assertion that every opinion has the same frequency or support.

distinctionTask.prompt: A broad spectrum of opinions means _____.
options: one identical view held by everyone
distinctionTask.explanation: Spectrum describes variation across the views.

originalSense.definition: A range; a continuous, infinite, one-dimensional set, possibly bounded by extremes.
originalSense.example: Near-synonyms: sliding scale, continuum

definition: No longer fresh.
example: The bread became stale after several days.
usage: Adjective describing lost freshness here. Other meanings concern overused ideas or information.
distinctions: Stale bread has lost freshness; the word alone does not establish whether it is safe or unsafe to eat.

distinctionTask.prompt: The bread is stale. This tells us that it _____.
distinctionTask.explanation: Stale describes freshness; it does not by itself establish toxicity.

originalSense.definition: No longer fresh, in reference to food, urine, straw, wounds, etc.
originalSense.example: Near-synonyms: gone bad, spoiled; see also Thesaurus:rotten

definition: A word or phrase with the same or a similar meaning to another in a particular use.
example: In "a large house", big is a synonym for large.
usage: Countable noun. Check the particular meaning, grammar and register before substituting one expression for another.
distinctions: Synonyms can overlap in a context without being interchangeable in every expression. Antonyms express opposing meanings.

distinctionTask.prompt: In "a large house", big is a synonym for large because the two describe _____.
distinctionTask.explanation: The adjective meanings overlap in the stated house context.

originalSense.definition: A term (word or phrase) which is synonymous with others.
originalSense.example: Near-synonyms: near-synonym, parasynonym, plesionym

definition: Material made from interlaced or matted fibres, whether woven or nonwoven.
example: The exhibit includes a textile made from woven plant fibres.
usage: Often used in the plural for materials or the industry. The source includes nonwoven materials as well as woven cloth.
distinctions: Textile is not restricted to woven fabric; matted-fibre materials are included in this source meaning.

distinctionTask.prompt: This meaning of textile includes _____.
distinctionTask.explanation: The source definition explicitly includes interlaced and matted fibres.

originalSense.definition: Any material made of interlacing or matted fibres, including carpeting and geotextiles, woven or nonwoven.
originalSense.example: Near-synonym: cloth (not always differentiated)

definition: A wide, shallow container used especially for cooking.
example: Heat the vegetables in a pan.
usage: Countable cooking-vessel noun. This everyday lowercase meaning is the default; the deity and other source meanings remain accessible.
distinctions: Pan here is the vessel. Pan with a capital P can be the Greek god's name in a separate source meaning.

distinctionTask.prompt: Heat the vegetables in a pan. Pan names _____.
distinctionTask.explanation: The food-heating context identifies the cooking noun.

originalSense.definition: A wide, flat receptacle used around the house, especially for cooking.

definition: An organisation established to carry out charitable work.
example: The charity provides meals for local families.
distinctions: A charity here is an organisation; charity can also name giving or help as an uncountable activity.
usage: Countable organisation noun: a charity, two charities.

originalSense.definition: An organization, the objective of which is to carry out a charitable purpose.
originalSense.example: ‘[…] I remember a lady coming to inspect St. Mary's Home where I was brought up and seeing us all in our lovely Elizabethan uniforms we were so proud of, and bursting into tears all over us because “it was wicked to dress us like charity children”.[…]’.

definition: Relating to the mind, including thought and emotion.
example: The puzzle requires considerable mental effort.
distinctions: Mental concerns the mind; physical concerns the body. A task may involve both.
usage: Adjective before a noun, as in mental effort.

originalSense.definition: Of or relating to the mind or specifically the total emotional and intellectual response of an individual to external reality.
originalSense.example: I don't mean all of your friends—only a small proportion—which, however, connects your circle with that deadly, idle, brainless bunch—the insolent chatterers at the opera,[…], the neurotic victims of mental cirrhosis, the jewelled animals whose moral code is the code of the barnyard—!

definition: Used to join words, phrases or clauses that are taken together.
example: The course includes reading and writing.
distinctions: And adds or combines items; or presents alternatives in a phrase such as tea or coffee.
usage: Coordinating conjunction. Join parallel items: reading and writing.

originalSense.definition: As a coordinating conjunction; expressing two elements to be taken together or in addition to each other.
originalSense.example: Soupes dorye. — Take gode almaunde mylke […] caste þher-to Safroun an Salt […]
wordFamily: South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands

definition: A strip of material used to cover or support a wound or injured body part.
example: The nurse wrapped a bandage around his wrist.
distinctions: A bandage is the material wrapped around an injury; a sling supports an arm in a different way.
usage: Countable noun: a bandage. To bandage is a separate verb.

originalSense.definition: A strip of gauze or similar material used to protect or support a wound or injury.
originalSense.example: […]he was deadly pale, and the blood-stained bandage round his head told that he had recently been wounded, and still more recently dressed.

definition: Physical or mental unease or distress.
example: The tight shoes caused considerable discomfort.
distinctions: Discomfort can be physical or mental; it does not always mean severe pain.
usage: Usually uncountable in this general meaning: some discomfort.

originalSense.definition: Mental or bodily distress.
originalSense.example: […] although overcrowding on the trains running via London Bridge has occasioned considerable discomfort to regular travellers, it was noticed that the alternative route was not extensively patronised, and that the trains were seldom more than half-filled.

definition: Supplying water to land to help plants grow.
example: The farm uses irrigation during dry weather.
distinctions: Irrigation supplies water to land; drainage removes excess water from it.
usage: Usually uncountable: irrigation, an irrigation system.

distinctionTask.prompt: The system supplies water to dry fields. It provides _____.
distinctionTask.explanation: Irrigation supplies water; drainage removes excess water.

originalSense.definition: The act or process of irrigating, or the state of being irrigated; especially, the operation of causing water to flow over lands, for nourishing plants.
originalSense.example: “My father had ideas about conservation long before the United States took it up.[…]You preserve water in times of flood and freshet to be used for power or for irrigation throughout the year. …”

definition: An area of land considered in terms of its visible natural and built features.
example: The mountain landscape changed as we travelled north.
distinctions: A landscape is the area and its features; a landscape painting is a representation of it.
usage: Countable noun for an area or view in this physical meaning.

originalSense.definition: A portion of land or territory as defined by its landform, its geographical (and architectural) features.
originalSense.example: Piſcat[or]. [...] [T]heſe Hills though high, bleak, and craggy, breed and feed good Beef, and Mutton above ground, and afford good ſtore of Lead within. / Viat[or]. They had need of all thoſe commodities to make amends for the ill Land-ſchape: [...]

definition: One of the breathing organs in which oxygen passes into the blood.
example: The scan showed damage to one lung.
distinctions: A lung is an organ involved in gas exchange; breathing is the process of moving air in and out.
usage: Countable noun: one lung, two lungs.

originalSense.definition: A biological organ of vertebrates that controls breathing and oxygenates the blood.
originalSense.example: I made a speaking trumpet of my hands and commenced to whoop “Ahoy!” and “Hello!” at the top of my lungs. […] The Colonel woke up, and, after asking what in brimstone was the matter, opened his mouth and roared “Hi!” and “Hello!” like the bull of Bashan.

definition: The legal state of owning something.
example: The records confirm her ownership of the house.
distinctions: Ownership is a legal relationship; possessing or using something does not by itself establish ownership.

distinctionTask.prompt: I borrowed the bicycle for a day. This alone establishes _____.
distinctionTask.explanation: Using or possessing borrowed property does not by itself make the borrower its owner.

originalSense.definition: The state of having complete legal control of something; possession; proprietorship.
originalSense.example: Other evidence of former ownerships such as notice-boards, number plates, and makers' plates, are often discovered unexpectedly. […] It has not been used for many years, and although it was impracticable to photograph the engine in the small confines of the shed it was possible to obtain a picture of the plate which it still carries showing the former ownership.

definition: A visual representation made by drawing, painting, printing or photography.
example: A picture of the old bridge hangs on the wall.
distinctions: Picture is broader than photograph: a drawing can also be a picture.
usage: Countable noun. Take a picture commonly means take a photograph.

distinctionTask.prompt: A child drew a tree with a pencil. The drawing is _____.
options: a picture but not a photograph
a photograph but not a picture
distinctionTask.answer: a picture but not a photograph
distinctionTask.explanation: Picture includes drawings; a photograph is made photographically.

originalSense.definition: A representation of anything (as a person, a landscape, a building) upon canvas, paper, or other surface, by drawing, painting, printing, photography, etc.
originalSense.example: Orion hit a rabbit once; but though sore wounded it got to the bury, and, struggling in, the arrow caught the side of the hole and was drawn out.[…]. Ikey the blacksmith had forged us a spearhead after a sketch from a picture of a Greek warrior; and a rake-handle served as a shaft.

definition: Something available for use in achieving a purpose.
example: Clean water is an essential resource for the village.
distinctions: A resource is something usable for a purpose; being a resource does not mean it is unlimited.
usage: Countable noun, often plural when discussing available materials, staff or funds.

originalSense.definition: Something that one uses to achieve an objective, e.g. raw materials or personnel.
originalSense.example: Nevertheless, it is clear that the global energy demand for air-conditioning will grow substantially as nations become more affluent,[…]. This trend will put additional strain not only on global energy resources but also on the environmental prospects of a warming planet.

definition: The compass direction halfway between south and west.
example: The wind is coming from the southwest.
distinctions: Southwest lies between south and west; southeast lies between south and east.
usage: Direction noun here. A wind from the southwest comes from that direction.

originalSense.definition: The intercardinal compass point halfway between south and west; specifically at a bearing of 225°.
originalSense.example: So this was my future home, I thought![…]Backed by towering hills, the but faintly discernible purple line of the French boundary off to the southwest, a sky of palest Gobelin flecked with fat, fleecy little clouds, it in truth looked a dear little city; the city of one's dreams.

definition: A hollow object with a cylindrical shape.
example: Water flowed through a narrow plastic tube.
distinctions: A tube has a hollow interior; a solid rod does not have that hollow form.

originalSense.definition: Anything that is hollow and cylindrical in shape.
originalSense.example: But then I had the [massive] flintlock by me for protection. ¶[…]The linen-press and a chest on the top of it formed, however, a very good gun-carriage; and, thus mounted, aim could be taken out of the window […], and a 'bead' could be drawn upon Molly, the dairymaid, kissing the fogger behind the hedge, little dreaming that the deadly tube was levelled at them.

definition: An enclosed motor vehicle used to carry goods or people.
example: The delivery van stopped outside the shop.
distinctions: Van identifies a type of vehicle; it does not specify one fixed capacity or size.
usage: Countable vehicle noun. Sizes and seating arrangements vary.

originalSense.definition: A covered motor vehicle used to carry goods or (normally less than ten) persons, usually roughly cuboid in shape, Depending on the type of van, it can be bigger or smaller than a pickup truck and SUV, and longer and higher than a car but relatively smaller than a truck/lorry or a bus.
originalSense.example: While Santa Monica has a longstanding prohibition against public camping that includes living in vehicles, the van rental business has been a problem in Venice for years. […] Organizations that provide safe parking locations have limited capacity and are often unable to accommodate the kind of non-operational vans that are being repurposed as makeshift housing.

definition: To sort things into groups according to their features or type.
example: The staff assort the samples by colour.
distinctions: Assort here means classify items; an assorted collection contains a mixture of different types.
usage: Transitive sorting verb, uncommon in ordinary conversation; sort is more usual.

originalSense.definition: To sort or arrange according to characteristic or class.
originalSense.example: They appear […] no way assorted to those with whom they must associate.

definition: A bag carried on the back with shoulder straps.
example: She packed her books in a backpack.
distinctions: A backpack is worn on the back; a suitcase is usually carried by a handle or moved on wheels.

originalSense.definition: A knapsack, sometimes mounted on a light frame, but always supported by straps, worn on a person’s back for the purpose of carrying things, especially when hiking, or on a student's back when carrying books.
originalSense.example: Rachel discovered that she could also keep things in her backpack that were important to her, nobody would know about them because they would be hidden. These important things included a small round rock that she had found […]

definition: A shore, especially one covered with sand or small stones.
example: We walked along the beach before breakfast.
distinctions: A beach can be beside a lake as well as the sea; coast usually concerns land along the sea.
usage: Countable noun. Use on the beach for location.

originalSense.definition: The shore of a body of water, especially when sandy or pebbly.
originalSense.example: Pretty soon I struck into a sort of path[…]. It twisted and turned,[…]and opened out into a big clear space like a lawn. And, back of the lawn, was a big, old-fashioned house, with piazzas stretching in front of it, and all blazing with lights. 'Twas the house I'd seen the roof of from the beach.

definition: A person who asks others for money or goods as help.
example: A beggar asked passers-by for money near the station.
distinctions: Beggar describes asking for help in this meaning; poverty alone does not mean someone begs.
usage: Countable person noun. Use neutral descriptions when discussing poverty.

originalSense.definition: A person who begs.
originalSense.example: “[…] They talk of you as if you were Croesus—and I expect the beggars sponge on you unconscionably.” And Vickers launched forth into a tirade very different from his platform utterances.
